bullets.section: What I’m absorbing (and aspiring to imitate) —
bullets.title: Eliza Ivanova’s Raw Material Volume 1
bullets.note: Eliza is an incredible artist and animator at Pixar. She was also one of the first artists I followed on Instagram ([@eleeza](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/opfkhq/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9lbGVlemEv)). I watch her time-lapse videos to think more deeply about drawing. This book is a collection of her work. I got the [custom cover edition](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/zvtghn/aHR0cHM6Ly9lbGVlemEuYmlnY2FydGVsLmNvbS9wcm9kdWN0L3Jhdy1tYXRlcmlhbC12LTEtY3VzdG9tLWNvdmVyLWVkaXRpb24=) (you get an original drawing of hers [like this](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/pnceh9/aHR0cHM6Ly9lbGVlemEuYmlnY2FydGVsLmNvbS9wcm9kdWN0L3Jhdy1tYXRlcmlhbC12LTEtY3VzdG9tLWNvdmVyLWVkaXRpb24=), and [here is mine](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/xksph6/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9wL0JpRFB2NEFBUy1iLz90YWtlbi1ieT10aW1mZXJyaXNz)), but [the regular hardcover](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/60aeh8/aHR0cHM6Ly9lbGVlemEuYmlnY2FydGVsLmNvbS9wcm9kdWN0L3Jhdy1tYXRlcmlhbC12LTEtaGFyZC1jb3Zlcg==) is also amazing.

bullets.title: Hu Kitchen cashew butter and pure vanilla dark chocolate bar
bullets.note: Be forewarned that you will eat entire bars at a time. If that’s sold out, I also love the [Qrispy dark chocolate](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/52hvh7/aHR0cHM6Ly9odWtpdGNoZW4uY29tL2NvbGxlY3Rpb25zL2Nob2NvbGF0ZS9wcm9kdWN0cy92YW5pbGxhLXF1aW5vYS1xcmlzcHk=).

bullets.title: Malemolência by Céu
bullets.note: ([@ceumusic](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/q3i8h7/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZmFjZWJvb2suY29tL2NldW11c2lj)). This has been one of my favorite songs for 2-3 years, and the entire album is stellar ([Lenda](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/gvfnh5/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj1zNW1wMGtWNlhXOA==) is another standout for me). The sexiness of the vocals is otherworldly. The [album cover pic](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/93tzhn/aHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnNwb3RpZnkuY29tL2FsYnVtLzZkRzFYUHJsMUtFZUs0TU5EN1dBb0I=) ain’t so bad, either. Oh, and [her videos](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/3wcphk/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj1RenF6SlJuN3BtYw==), too.

bullets.title: Musicophilia: Tales of Music and the Brain
bullets.creator: Oliver Sacks
bullets.note: I’m diving deeply into music, and this book combines that new interest with neuroscience, mostly through the lens of unusual (and often spectacular) pathologies. Here’s the short description from Amazon: “With the same trademark compassion and erudition he brought to [_The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat_](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/lmun74z88amh4p869/43avhe/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYW1hem9uLmNvbS9NYW4tV2hvLU1pc3Rvb2stSGlzLVdpZmUvZHAvMTQxNjU0Mjc4Nw==), Oliver Sacks explores the place music occupies in the brain and how it affects the human condition. In _Musicophilia_, he shows us a variety of what he calls ‘musical misalignments.’ Among them: a man struck by lightning who suddenly desires to become a pianist at the age of forty-two; an entire group of children with Williams syndrome, who are hypermusical from birth; people with ‘amusia,’ to whom a symphony sounds like the clattering of pots and pans; and a man whose memory spans only seven seconds--for everything but music.”
